format.note: Fields are present, examples are concrete, and observability labels distinguish proposed static checks from reviewer judgment. However, activation.facts does not match given/when: task_term requires particular vocabulary, and operation/finding describe existing violations, while given/when covers any subset read and optional persistence, including new implementations without those violations. The integration layer is also listed although given names only use cases and route handlers.

generality.note: The bounded-history-cost rule and its examples transfer across applications and business domains.

decisionUseful.note: Coder-facing guidance specifies indexed subset queries, adapter additions, changed-record writes, batched reads, and the prohibited scanning patterns.

requiredFixes: Align activation.facts with given/when: express the subset-read request context as the trigger, and keep violation operations, history-growth findings, and vocabulary hints as detection aids rather than additional applicability requirements. Ensure a new subset-query implementation can activate without an existing violation or particular task words.

Clarify integration-layer applicability consistently in activation and given: either include adapters supporting the described request path in given, or limit activation to the handler/use-case context.
summary: The convention faithfully captures the specification's single bounded-request-cost obligation, including its read, write, and evidence requirements. Its activation metadata needs alignment with the broader coder-facing trigger before it passes.
